claims.text: Unmodified TC4 (Ti6Al4V) has an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase structure.
Unmodified TC4 has low hardness and poor wear resistance.
The proposed treatment uses an approximately 50–100 nm Ti interlayer followed by a 1–2 micrometer DLC coating deposited by PVD.
Keeping the substrate below 200 degrees Celsius during deposition will prevent changes to TC4's underlying dual-phase microstructure.
The treatment will produce a uniform and adherent Ti-interlayer/DLC multilayer surface.
The Ti interlayer promotes strong adhesion between TC4 and the DLC coating.
The Ti interlayer will provide robust bonding under high-contact-stress conditions.
DLC has high hardness and a low coefficient of friction.
The DLC layer acts as a wear-resistant barrier.
The multilayer coating minimizes metal-to-metal contact and thereby reduces friction and wear.
The low-temperature surface treatment preserves TC4's intrinsic bulk mechanical properties and beneficial alpha-plus-beta microstructure.
Relative to untreated TC4, the coating will reduce the coefficient of friction by up to approximately 50 percent.
Relative to untreated TC4, the coating will increase surface hardness by approximately 30–60 percent.
The coating will improve wear resistance and prolong service life under extreme-service conditions.
The intervention is applicable under high-contact-stress and extreme-service conditions if adhesion, thickness uniformity, and low-temperature processing are maintained.
Excessive thermal cycling or mechanical shock may degrade coating performance.
Prior evidence supports improved tribological performance from DLC coatings.
Long-term adhesion stability under extreme cyclic loading and environmental variation in TC4 remains uncertain.
Interlayer thickness and deposition parameters may require further optimization.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis permits a DLC thickness of 1–2 micrometers, including exactly 2 micrometers, whereas the intervention specifies a coating thinner than 2 micrometers.
